searchText: Hello! I'm trying to deploy a smart contract for testing EIP-7002 but I can't. Any suggestions please? many thanks! What are you trying to do? Just a final validation of the smart contract. Just want to deploy it, create a few validators with the withdrawal credentials pointing to that SC and, after that, trigger the exits The contract already exists in pectra-devnet-6, so feel free to use it: https://pectra-devnet-6.ethpandaops.io/ great! many thanks! Apologies because I'm sure I've seen the link before, but please could someone point me to the source code for the contract that supports EIP-7002 (`0x00000961Ef480Eb55e80D19ad83579A64c007002`)? (And lower priority, but it would be nice if the deployment process for devnets added the contract source to the explorers.) https://github.com/lightclient/sys-asm It's in here: - <https://github.com/lightclient/sys-asm/tree/main/src/withdrawals> - <https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7002> Deployment is in here: - <https://github.com/ethpandaops/ethereum-genesis-generator/blob/master/apps/el-gen/genesis_geth.py#L113> There are a few app implementations around and we've been working on some if you need help with calling it. - Dora: <https://github.com/ethpandaops/dora/blob/f844d0371e8f81b04982e0916112a3c87907dbf1/ui-package/src/components/SubmitWithdrawalsForm/WithdrawalReview.tsx#L296> - WIP Launchpad update: <https://github.com/ethereum/staking-launchpad/blob/pectra/src/pages/Actions/components/PartialWithdraw.tsx#L81> The important parts are: > Withdrawal Request Contract > The contract has three different code paths, which can be summarized at a high level as follows: > > 1. Add withdrawal request - requires a 56 byte input, the validator’s public key concatenated with a big-endian uint64 amount value. > 2. Fee getter - if the input length is zero, return the current fee required to add a withdrawal request. > 3. System process - if called by system address, pop off the withdrawal requests for the current block from the queue. > And lower priority, but it would be nice if the deployment process for devnets added the contract source to the explorers There is no higher level source code 😄 so nothing to verify in explorers From the looks of things `amount` in EIP-7002 is a gwei amount, as opposed to a wei amount. This information isn't present in the EIP, but am I correct in this assumption? We use `amount * 1000000000` where amount is in ETH so it would mean the amount is in gwei. Trial and error discovery for me 😄 (Too late to change, I'm sure, but using the amount `0` for exiting the validator seems to be a poor choice; I'm sure that it would be relatively easy to accidentally create a withdrawal request with this value (I've already managed it 🤣 ). I'll put guards in `ethereal` to avoid this, but I can see many people slipping up here.) Dedaub audit seems to have it in wei (unless I am misreading table) - see p. 4 https://github.com/ethereum/audits/blob/master/Pectra/Dedaub%20-%20EIP7002.pdf unrelated question, and possibly dumb, but is it intended that you can activate a validator with 0x02 creds? [the least elegant way to do this would be to manually change the beginning from 01 to 02 in the deposit file...but maybe I am missing something) one more question - hoping someone can confirm - for active validations, you cannot consolidate two 0x01 validators - is that correct? It is intended that you first obtain 0x02 credentials for the target validator and then you can consolidate other validators (including 0x01) into that 0x02 - is that correct? You can deposit for a new validator with `0x02` withdrawal credentials, yes. That is correct. You can upgrade a `0x01` in-place to a `0x02` with the consolidation request using source==target or you can do a consolidation request only if the target is a `0x02` and the source is either a `0x01` or a `0x02`. Thank you! Very much appreciated! Why is the `state_root` when querying the beacon state object API on mekong `0x00000....` Is there an issue? Making the following call: ``` curl -v -X GET 'https://beacon.mekong.ethpandaops.io:443/eth/v2/debug/beacon/states/654720' \ -H 'accept: application/json' \ --output beacon_654720.json ``` That's expected. You can't have the current state root within the state 😉 Am I correct in thinking that the withdrawal contract only takes a single withdrawal? So if someone wants to send multiple withdrawals we're going to have to write a separate batch contract? batch contracts won't work as the sender of the request needs to be the withdrawal address. you could do batching with 7702 tho.. but yea, each call to the system contract includes one withdrawal request only good day <@808969530608451584> At ~85k gas per tx that's not cheap, but okay. I haven't played with 7702 so may take a look. gas usage is also not easily predictable 😅 first request in each block is more expensive than the rest Gas estimation should always give the more expensive option, so that's "good" in that the tx is less likely to revert from being out of gas. yeaa, unfortunately the gas estimation knows about previous transactions when trying to do batches. so the estimation for subsequent transactions is lower, which might not work if part of the batch slips into the next block 😅 I've ended up setting a static gas limit for requests submitted through dora.. <@710132892197453824> also spent a lot time with batching multiple requests, he might have another solution

excerpts.author: remyroy
excerpts.content:
It's in here:
- <https://github.com/lightclient/sys-asm/tree/main/src/withdrawals>
- <https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7002>

Deployment is in here:
- <https://github.com/ethpandaops/ethereum-genesis-generator/blob/master/apps/el-gen/genesis_geth.py#L113>

There are a few app implementations around and we've been working on some if you need help with calling it.

- Dora: <https://github.com/ethpandaops/dora/blob/f844d0371e8f81b04982e0916112a3c87907dbf1/ui-package/src/components/SubmitWithdrawalsForm/WithdrawalReview.tsx#L296>
- WIP Launchpad update: <https://github.com/ethereum/staking-launchpad/blob/pectra/src/pages/Actions/components/PartialWithdraw.tsx#L81>

The important parts are:

> Withdrawal Request Contract
> The contract has three different code paths, which can be summarized at a high level as follows:
> 
> 1. Add withdrawal request - requires a 56 byte input, the validator’s public key concatenated with a big-endian uint64 amount value.
> 2. Fee getter - if the input length is zero, return the current fee required to add a withdrawal request.
> 3. System process - if called by system address, pop off the withdrawal requests for the current block from the queue.

excerpts.author: jgm
excerpts.content: From the looks of things `amount` in EIP-7002 is a gwei amount, as opposed to a wei amount.  This information isn't present in the EIP, but am I correct in this assumption?

excerpts.author: remyroy
excerpts.content: We use `amount * 1000000000` where amount is in ETH so it would mean the amount is in gwei.

excerpts.author: remyroy
excerpts.content: Trial and error discovery for me 😄

excerpts.author: jgm
excerpts.content: (Too late to change, I'm sure, but using the amount `0`  for exiting the validator seems to be a poor choice; I'm sure that it would be relatively easy to accidentally create a withdrawal request with this value (I've already managed it 🤣 ).  I'll put guards in `ethereal` to avoid this, but I can see many people slipping up here.)

excerpts.author: builder_benny
excerpts.content: Dedaub audit seems to have it in wei (unless I am misreading table) - see p. 4 https://github.com/ethereum/audits/blob/master/Pectra/Dedaub%20-%20EIP7002.pdf

excerpts.author: builder_benny
excerpts.content: unrelated question, and possibly dumb, but is it intended that you can activate a validator with 0x02 creds? [the least elegant way to do this would be to manually change the beginning from 01 to 02 in the deposit file...but maybe I am missing something)

excerpts.author: builder_benny
excerpts.content:
one more question - hoping someone can confirm - for active validations, you cannot consolidate two 0x01 validators - is that correct? 

It is intended that you first obtain 0x02 credentials for the target validator and then you can consolidate other validators (including 0x01) into that 0x02 - is that correct?

excerpts.author: remyroy
excerpts.content: You can deposit for a new validator with `0x02` withdrawal credentials, yes.

excerpts.author: remyroy
excerpts.content: That is correct. You can upgrade a `0x01` in-place to a `0x02` with the consolidation request using source==target or you can do a consolidation request only if the target is a `0x02` and the source is either a `0x01` or a `0x02`.

excerpts.author: builder_benny
excerpts.content: Thank you! Very much appreciated!

excerpts.author: yash99
excerpts.content:
Why is the `state_root` when querying the beacon state object API on mekong `0x00000....` Is there an issue? 

Making the following call: 

```
curl -v -X GET 'https://beacon.mekong.ethpandaops.io:443/eth/v2/debug/beacon/states/654720' \
-H 'accept: application/json' \
--output beacon_654720.json
```

excerpts.author: pk910
excerpts.content: That's expected. You can't have the current state root within the state 😉

excerpts.author: jgm
excerpts.content: Am I correct in thinking that the withdrawal contract only takes a single withdrawal?  So if someone wants to send multiple withdrawals we're going to have to write a separate batch contract?

excerpts.author: pk910
excerpts.content:
batch contracts won't work as the sender of the request needs to be the withdrawal address.
you could do batching with 7702 tho..

excerpts.author: pk910
excerpts.content: but yea,  each call to the system contract includes one withdrawal request only

excerpts.author: jgm
excerpts.content: At ~85k gas per tx that's not cheap, but okay.  I haven't played with 7702 so may take a look.

excerpts.author: pk910
excerpts.content:
gas usage is also not easily predictable 😅  
first request in each block is more expensive than the rest

excerpts.author: jgm
excerpts.content: Gas estimation should always give the more expensive option, so that's "good" in that the tx is less likely to revert from being out of gas.

excerpts.author: pk910
excerpts.content:
yeaa, unfortunately the gas estimation knows about previous transactions when trying to do batches. 
so the estimation for subsequent transactions is lower, which might not work if part of the batch slips into the next block 😅 
I've ended up setting a static gas limit for requests submitted through dora..
<@710132892197453824> also spent a lot time with batching multiple requests, he might have another solution
